_doc: Rail model for tools/verify/pdn_ir.py (DC IR drop on the real copper) and tools/verify/thermal_board.py.
Every rail of tools/power_widths.json has an entry. Names use the table spelling ('/'); the solver matches the board's '{slash}' spelling.
sources: pads held at the nominal voltage (regulator / switch / eFuse OUT pins, shunt output pads, inductor output pads, or the input connector pin).
loads: per reference designator. 'pins' = list of pad numbers or '*' (all pads of that ref on the rail). 'w' = relative weight (A) used to distribute
the case total over the loads; 'amps' = absolute current (not scaled). A group's current is split EQUALLY over its pads (no tie through the part:
conservative, avoids inventing a conduction path through a component). 'budget_mv' on a load overrides the rail budget for that load.
auto_power_in_a: every power_in pad on the rail not listed as a source or load gets this weight (DRAFT logic allowance); passives and inputs draw 0.
cases: 'design' = loads scaled so their sum equals total_a (default: power_widths.json amps). Extra cases list absolute currents.
Budgets are DRAFT unless 'budget_class' says otherwise; the justification is in 'budget_basis'. Citations: keys of the 'citations' table.
Loads are design assumptions taken from the documents cited, NOT measurements.

_doc_hot_parts: hot_parts: parts whose dissipation thermal_board.py injects into their own pads (side layer). model: efficiency (vout x iout x (1/eta - 1) x ic_share), i2r (i_a^2 x R(T_J) table + extra_w), ldo ((vin - vout) x iout + vin x iq), fixed (p_w). T_J = mean model temperature of the heated pads + psi_c_per_w x P; tj_max_c = datasheet limit (null = not judged). rails: the part's power rails; NOT_ROUTED loads on them make the part record NOT_ROUTED unless it already FAILs. All currents are design assumptions (cited), not measurements.
